memory_candidates.content: Documentation-drift tasks converge fastest under a three-owner policy: (1) machine-checkable facts (axiom sets, sorry-freeness) owned by the invariant checker's pinned baseline; (2) counts owned by a generator that writes BEGIN/END GENERATED blocks in place, keyed on filename so hand-written Description columns survive regeneration; (3) per-item status owned by exactly one ledger file, with every other surface reduced to a pointer plus a <=5-row highlights table. The non-obvious constraint is the description carry-across: a naive regenerator destroys the best documentation in the tree, so the generator must regenerate mechanical columns only. A second recurring finding: every grep-derived count in a stale-documentation task description came out HIGHER when re-derived (one by 85x), so plan phases should treat any inherited count as a lower bound and re-derive at phase start.
